text:
miranda: FYI we're doing bring-up of Prism-7B-lite (FP16 -> 4-bit GPTQ) on Dedicated. Benchmarks look great for chat latency, but we hit a weird licensing note. Need legal eyeballs before any external hosting.

oliver: quick numbers: p50 latency down 45%, p95 down 38%. perf delta on our summarization eval: -2.1% BLEU-esque metric, but hallucination rate +0.6% on constrained Q/A. Can mitigate with prompt fixes.

miranda: pasted the license snippet from upstream repo below. curious whether "service aggregation" clause means we can't host a quantized variant behind an API.

infra-bot: ```
PRISM MODEL LICENSE v2.0
- Allowed: research, evaluation, and local noncommercial deployment.
- Prohibited: direct commercial hosting, sale, or distribution of model binaries.
- Service Aggregation: providing access to model functionality as part of a paid service (including API endpoints) requires express commercial licensing.
- Transformations: "Converted, compressed, or quantized formats derived from the Model are considered Derivative Works unless otherwise agreed."
- Attribution: All Derivative Works must include a visible attribution including upstream model name and license URI.
```

priya (legal): summary: there are two potential blockers: (1) the Service Aggregation clause likely covers hosted API for paying customers, and (2) the Transformations line explicitly calls quantized formats "Derivative Works". That would mean redistribution/hosting needs permission and attribution.

oliver: technical nuance: our pipeline doesn't publish the quantized binary. We serve in-memory quant tensors via inference runtime. Does "distribution of binaries" differ from "serving via API"?

priya (legal): legally the license distinguishes both. "Distribution of model binaries" is one prohibition, and "service aggregation" covers API hosting. Even if you never hand out the binary file, serving model outputs to paying users looks like a commercial service.

sam: product question: could we offer the quantized variant under Dedicated where the customer brings their own license (BYOL) and we provide runtime? That usually avoids hosting the model for them.

priya (legal): BYOL is a good fallback but still tricky: if we host the runtime with their binary uploaded to our infra, that might still be considered hosting the model. Better: customer supplies the model and runs it inside their VPC/Private deployment where we don't control or distribute the model. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed), we'd need permission.

miranda: actionably, we can keep the quantized variant for internal benchmarking and Private-only demos. No public/revenue routes until clearance.

oliver: also need to call out attribution UX: upstream requires visible attribution and license URI in derivative works. Is adding a model card in Console + tooltip credit in UI sufficient?

priya (legal): usually yes: a persistent model metadata card that contains "Powered by Prism-7B-lite (Prism Research) — see [license link]" plus the redistribution notice in the legal page should satisfy attribution. We'll confirm in outreach.

sam: outreach ask to upstream should include: (1) permission to host quantized runtime for paying customers on Redwood-managed Dedicated, (2) permission to keep runtime internal but serve outputs, (3) exact attribution language they require, and (4) any revenue/usage terms.

infra-bot: policy: tag onboarding entry "legal:pending", set "hosted:blocked".

miranda: I'll attach profiling and the exact GPTQ commit + checksum to the onboarding folder. Also will include our rollback plan: auto-fallback to FP16 if quality degradation > 5% or hallucination increases by +2%.

oliver: technical note for outreach: mention we don't publish quantized artifacts externally, quant format is GPTQ v1 frame, chunked shards encrypted at rest, and we can implement attribution banners and rate-limits. Add that we can sign an indemnity clause if needed.

priya (legal): legal action items: 1) miranda upload upstream license + hash; 2) sam/priya draft outreach template and propose attribution string; 3) oliver detail quant pipeline + storage/ship policy; 4) product prepare fallback messaging and BYOL doc. We'll sync Wed.

miranda: done — files uploaded to /onboard/prism-7b-lite. pinging @priya when draft ready. :thumbsup:

sam: if upstream declines commercial hosting, we'll surface BYOL + Private deployment as the supported path and mark model as "hosted:ineligible" in the catalog.

miranda: thanks everyone. leaving thread open for followups.
